title: SEMA-Bound Outlander Diamond Trail Edition Channels Mitsubishi’s Off-Road Roots

body_markdown:
Earlier in 2026, Mitsubishi[announced plans](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/new-mitsubishi-models-pickup-launch-date/) to launch several new models on the American market by 2030. It’s returning to the SEMA show for the first time since 2012 to unveil one of its upcoming cars. The new 2028 Mitsubishi Outlander Diamond Trail Edition is a factory-built off-roader that features rugged, edition-specific styling, all-terrain tires, and an off-road driving profile.


Returning to SEMA helps Mitsubishi reposition itself as an outdoorsy, enthusiast-focused brand after years of flying under the radar, and the Outlander Diamond Trail Edition certainly looks ready to venture off the beaten path. It stands out from other trim levels with black exterior cladding, trim-specific 18-inch wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires, and raised roof rails. The lower-profile bumpers increase the approach angle from 18.3 to 20.5 degrees and the departure angle from 22.2 to 23.1 degrees.


Trail Green Metallic was created specifically for the Diamond Trail Edition, and you can order it with a contrasting white roof panel for a touch of vintage flair. Inside, you’ll find gray water-repellent upholstery with khaki stitching and trim-specific accents.


This is more of a soft-roader than an off-roader that can keep up with[a Wrangler](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/the-2027-wrangler-jl-2a-harkens-back-to-jeeps-first-civilian-focused-model/) in Moab, but the changes aren’t only skin-deep. Mitsubishi explains that it added a driving profile called Rock that improves traction by stopping wheel spin almost immediately. This mode reacts faster than the existing driving profiles, and it’s part of the S-AWC all-wheel-drive system that comes standard.


Rock Mode automatically engages hill descent control, and the driver can configure the instrument cluster to show an off-road-oriented menu that provides information such as steering angle, individual wheel slip, and traction control intervention. Another feature inaugurated by the Diamond Trail Edition is a multi-view camera system that can be activated at up to 18.6 mph, up from 6.2 mph in the regular Outlander. These features should give drivers some peace of mind if they end up off the beaten path.


Mitsubishi will display three variants of the Outlander Diamond Trail Edition at SEMA. Shown below, the trio consists of a model modified with a selection of Mitsubishi accessories, one with more modifications (including a 1.5-inch lift kit) and a trailer, and one with extensive modifications such as a 2.5-inch lift kit, a roof-mounted tent, and light bars. Older concepts will be shown, too, but it doesn’t sound like[the new Montero](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/all-new-mitsubishi-pajero-looks-capable-but-will-we-get-it-stateside/) will travel to Sin City. Mitsubishi still hasn’t decided whether it will sell the SUV here.


The new 2028 Mitsubishi Outlander Diamond Trail Edition will make its debut at the 2026 SEMA show on November 3, 2026. It will go on sale nationwide shortly after, though pricing and availability haven’t been announced yet.[As usual](https://www.hagerty.com/media/events/gallery-recapping-sema-2025/) , *Hagerty* will be on the ground at the Las Vegas Convention Center to bring you live images and the latest updates from SEMA. Stay tuned for more.
